title: Fit a camera to a sphere or box
purpose: Frame a bounding sphere or box with a three.js camera: the sphere distance for the narrower field of view, a tight perspective box fit from any direction with a margin and near and far planes around the box, an orthographic fit, and a helper that applies it. Use it for viewers, thumbnails and focus on selection.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: The fits need no three.js; applyFit sets fields of a three.js PerspectiveCamera or OrthographicCamera (any recent release). Only 0.186.1 was run.

exports.name: fitSphereDistance
exports.summary: radius / sin(half), half the narrower of the vertical and horizontal half-angles.

exports.name: fitBoxPerspective
exports.signature: fitBoxPerspective(min, max, fovDegrees, aspect, options = {}) -> {position, target, up, distance, near, far}
exports.summary: Tight perspective fit of a box from a view direction; one corner touches the frame shrunk by margin.

exports.name: fitBoxOrthographic
exports.signature: fitBoxOrthographic(min, max, aspect, options = {}) -> {position, target, up, left, right, top, bottom, near, far}
exports.summary: Orthographic fit of a box with the given aspect.

exports.name: applyFit
exports.summary: Set position, up, look-at, near, far, orthographic extents and zoom 1, then updateProjectionMatrix.

exports.name: FIT_CAMERA_DEFAULTS
exports.summary: Frozen default options: direction, up, margin, depthPadding.

options.name: direction
options.meaning: Where the camera looks, from the camera toward the box.

options.name: up
options.meaning: Up hint; replaced when parallel to the direction.

options.name: margin
options.meaning: At least 1; the box fills 1 / margin of the frame.

options.name: depthPadding
options.meaning: At least 1; widens near and far around the box.

limits: The camera always looks at the box centre: the fit is tight for that aim, not the smallest frame over every possible aim. Boxes are axis-aligned in world space; a rotated object gets the loose box of its rotated bounds. The sphere distance ignores where the sphere sits off-axis. applyFit resets zoom to 1 and sets up, so a camera with roll or zoom changes. No animation: pair it with a spring to move smoothly. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run for the demo, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Sphere tangent to the narrower half field of view, d = r / sin(half)
Per-corner distance bound |x| / tan(half) - z in the camera basis
Orthographic extents widened to the viewport aspect
